faq.a: Siamak is associated with the Persian form سِيَامَك, whose core sense is siamak; a persian legendary figure.

faq.q: What is the origin of Siamak?
faq.a: Siamak is associated with Persian. Siamak is Persian سیامک (Siyāmak), the name of a figure in the Shahnameh. It is used as a male given name in Iran.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Siamak can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Siamak should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Siyāmak is a Persian name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Siamak mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Siamak is rendered سیامک and carries the sense سیامک، چهره افسانه‌ای.
A romanized syllable approximation is sia-mak. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Siamak?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Siamak, siamak. Script forms are سيامک, سِيَامَك, سیامک, सियामक.

faq.q: Is Siamak a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
